text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) said the government was plotting to assassinate its leader Chakufwa Chihana who announced he would use the constitution to force early general elections. The ruling United Demoractic Front (UDF) dismissed the claim.

- Police inspector Patrick Chikapa was served with a final order to appear in the high court after failing to appear in court on Wednesday for allegedly ordering his deputy to ignore a summons charging him with contempt of court.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and three other parties not represented in parliament have called for an urgent conference on the review of the constitution.

- Blantyre-based lawyer Viva Nyimba has complained to Attorney-General Cassim Chilumpha that police officers were behaving like they were in a police state where no person could question their authority.
